newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank victory seen strengthening hand on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank victory seen strengthening hand on EMU.

text.p: The Bundesbank has shown its power in forcing Bonn to back down in a battle over revaluing assets and greatly strengthened its hand in influencing the shape of economic and monetary union, financial analysts say.
"This may look like a compromise but it's not. The Bundesbank won. (Finance Minister Theo) Waigel caved in," John Butler, senior fixed income analyst at WestLB in Duesseldorf, said on Wednesday.
"This demonstrates what the Bundesbank is capable of."
According to its law, the central bank can offer advice on Germany's entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Analysts said such public advice was unlikely before recommendations were made in the spring of 1998 on which countries would be in the first round making the grade for a single euro currency.
But the bank's hand has been strengthened a lot in the run-up to that point, they said.
The Bonn government has abandoned earlier plans to take a one-off profit this year on reserve revaluations in order to meet the EMU criteria.
